costGuide.labourLine: Fitting an OM602 engine typically takes 10-14 hours at £65-£85/hr (independent) - confirm exact labour when comparing quotes.

failures.title: Mercedes-Benz OM602 Engine Problems - What Actually Fails

items.title: Timing Chain Stretch - All variants, especially commercial
items.whatHappens: The timing chain can stretch over high mileage, leading to a distinct rattling noise on cold starts. If ignored, it can jump a tooth, causing valve-to-piston contact and catastrophic engine failure.
items.repairVsReplace: If caught early, a timing chain kit replacement is straightforward and cost-effective. If the engine has already suffered valve damage, a full reconditioned unit is the only viable path.

items.title: Injector Seal Weeping ("Black Death") - All variants
items.whatHappens: The copper washer seals at the base of the injectors degrade over time, allowing combustion gases to escape. This creates a black, crusty carbon buildup around the injector heads and can lead to difficult cold starts or rough idling.
items.repairVsReplace: This is a routine maintenance item, not a terminal failure. Replacing the seals and cleaning the head is inexpensive and should be done preventatively.

items.title: Vacuum Pump and Turbocharger Wear - .960 and .980 variants
items.whatHappens: The brake servo vacuum pump is driven off the camshaft and can develop internal leaks, while the turbochargers on the 2.5T and 2.9T variants are prone to shaft play and oil seal degradation over time.
items.repairVsReplace: Both are replaceable components. A failing vacuum pump is a cheap fix, while a reconditioned turbocharger is the recommended route for boost issues.

failures.goodYearsLine: The OM602 is widely regarded as one of Mercedes’ most robust diesel engines, often outlasting the OM617 it succeeded in daily drivability. Units maintained with regular oil changes routinely exceed 300,000 miles without major internal issues .

variants.title: OM602 Sub-Codes Explained - Which One Is in Your Car?
variants.intro: INTRO: The OM602 family shares the same fundamental 5-cylinder block and pre-chamber head design, but displacement and forced induction vary depending on the chassis. Identifying your exact sub-code ensures you order the correct injection pump, turbo, and ancillary components. - Fitted to: 190-Class W201 (190D 2.5), E-Class W124 (250D) - Key technical difference: The base naturally aspirated variant, featuring a specific 2.5L crankshaft and simpler ancillary layout without turbo plumbing. - Sub-code-specific failure note: Shares the family failure pattern above; no unique widespread defects. - Interchange note: Not a straight swap with the turbo variants; the injection pump, exhaust manifold, and oil return lines differ significantly. - Fitted to: E-Class W124 (250D Turbo) - Key technical difference: Adds a turbocharger and intercooler to the 2.5L block, requiring a higher-capacity mechanical injection pump and revised piston cooling jets. - Sub-code-specific failure note: Shares the family failure pattern above; turbocharger shaft wear is the primary additional wear item. - Interchange note: Can be swapped with the .940 block, but requires the complete turbo kit, different injection pump, and revised engine management linkages. - Fitted to: T1 Vans (210D, 310D), Vario (512D, 612D), Sprinter 901/902/903/904 (212D) - Key technical difference: Increased displacement to 2.9L for higher low-end torque, making it the definitive choice for light and medium commercial applications. - Sub-code-specific failure note: Shares the family failure pattern above; commercial variants may experience earlier vacuum pump wear due to higher idle hours and heavier loads. - Interchange note: The passenger car and van versions share the same core architecture, but the sump, oil pickup, accessory brackets, and flywheel are application-specific.

buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement OM602 Engine - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: A used OM602 engine makes sense only if it comes with verifiable service history and a recent timing chain replacement. Given the age of these vehicles, the primary risk is hidden corrosion or degraded rubber seals, so a compression test is mandatory before purchase.

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: A proper reconditioned OM602 engine is the sweet spot for most buyers. A reputable rebuild will address the common failure points by fitting a new timing chain kit, updated injector seals, and a refreshed mechanical injection pump, giving the engine a fresh lease on life.

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: A full OM602 engine rebuild is justified for high-mileage commercial vans or classic W124 restorations where originality and maximum longevity are required. An upgraded rebuild should include line-boring the block, new pistons/rings, and a balanced crankshaft.

buyingGuide.supplyFitLine: Sourcing and fitting through our vetted network ensures your OM602 engine is installed by specialists familiar with classic Mercedes mechanical diesels, backed by a nationwide warranty.
buyingGuide.vehicleValueNote: Because the OM602 is typically found in vehicles valued between £1,500 and £8,000 (with classic W124s sometimes commanding higher premiums), a full replacement can represent a significant portion of the car's worth. If the lowest viable replacement cost exceeds approximately 60% of the vehicle's current market value, evaluate scrap value before committing .

items.question: How much does a Mercedes OM602 engine replacement cost?
items.answer: A reconditioned Mercedes OM602 engine typically costs between £1,500 and £2,500 for supply only . Fitted costs generally range from £2,200 to £3,300 depending on the specialist, while used units can be found from £500 but carry higher risk due to the engine's age. Compare OM602 engine replacement quotes today

items.question: What is the most common failure on the OM602 engine?
items.answer: The most documented issues are timing chain stretch and injector seal weeping, often referred to as "Black Death". Timing chain rattle on cold starts is the primary warning sign of stretch, which can lead to catastrophic valve damage if ignored, whereas injector seal failure causes black carbon buildup around the injector heads and rough idling but is a cheap and routine fix. Get quotes for a rebuilt OM602 with these issues resolved

items.question: Which Mercedes models use the OM602 engine?
items.answer: The OM602 was fitted to the W201 190-Class (190D 2.5), the W124 E-Class (250D and 250D Turbo), and early commercial vans including the T1, Vario, and first-generation Sprinter models. Check your registration to confirm your exact OM602 fitment

items.question: Should I buy a used or reconditioned OM602 engine?
items.answer: A reconditioned OM602 is strongly recommended over a used unit due to the age of these vehicles. A proper rebuild will replace the timing chain, tensioner, and injector seals, eliminating the two most common failure points, whereas used engines may appear cheaper upfront but often hide degraded rubber seals and stretched chains that will fail shortly after installation. Compare reconditioned OM602 engine prices from UK specialists

items.question: What is the difference between OM602.940, .960, and .980?
items.answer: The OM602.940 is the 2.5L naturally aspirated variant found in passenger cars, the OM602.960 is the 2.5L turbocharged version, and the OM602.980 is the 2.9L turbocharged variant calibrated for heavier commercial van applications; they share the same core block, but the injection pumps, sumps, and accessory brackets are not always directly interchangeable without modification.
